plans.note: Article headed INDEMNIFICATION; LIABILITY; INSURANCE is the natural home for a consequential-damages waiver and any aggregate cap. Check for mutuality and whether carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality breach, willful misconduct, IP infringement) are balanced; collaboration agreements often waive consequentials with no monetary cap, which is acceptable only if mutual.

Look in sec-p0580 for RevMed's indemnity to Sanofi (third-party IP claims arising from RevMed Background/Licensed Technology, breach of its reps in sec-p0536, and its own negligence/willful misconduct) and confirm Sanofi's reciprocal indemnity is confined to its own development/commercialization conduct. Cross-check third-party infringement handling in the IP article.

Defined terms Competing Product, Other SHP2 Inhibitor, Non-SHP2 Same Class Product and Immuno-Oncology Agent signal a field-restriction/non-compete covenant likely in the LICENSE article or in the covenants (sec-13.3 covers RevMed's side; any Sanofi-side covenant would sit in the same article, sec-p0536). Assess scope, duration and product/class breadth of any restriction on Sanofi's own or in-licensed programs; carve-outs for Acquiror Family/Acquired Party Family suggest a Change of Control-linked competition clause.

Two directions to test: (i) exclusivity of the licence granted to us in sec-p0246 (in our favour, do not flag) and (ii) any obligation on Sanofi to source Product only from RevMed under MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (sec-p0357) or to work exclusively with RevMed on SHP2 Inhibitors under the covenants. Only supplier-side lock-in on us is a candidate deviation.

No defined term or heading suggests most-favoured-nation pricing. Sweep FINANCIAL PROVISIONS (royalty/Royalty Floor, milestone and Manufacturing Costs terms) and the supply article for any 'terms no less favourable' language; if none, mark missing/not applicable rather than redlining.

Employee non-solicits in collaboration agreements, if present, sit in GENERAL PROVISIONS or alongside the covenants. Scan sec-p0605 for a no-hire/non-solicit; if found, check duration and general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out, and that it binds both parties.

TERM AND TERMINATION should contain Sanofi's at-will termination right (notice period, whether per-Product/per-country, any termination fee or continuing milestone/royalty obligation) and RevMed's termination rights. Confirm RevMed cannot terminate for convenience mid-Term and that our notice period is workable without penalty.

Term is defined and likely runs to expiry of royalty obligations rather than a renewing subscription term; check sec-p0484 for any automatic extension and notice window. Expect no auto-renewal mechanic — note as not applicable rather than a deviation.

GENERAL PROVISIONS will carry governing law, dispute escalation to the Designated Senior Officers and forum. Verify the law is New York/Delaware/California/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts (or, if arbitration, that seat and rules are US-based); note escalation-only steps in the rationale.

Check the assignment clause in sec-p0605 for our right to assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger without consent, and whether RevMed obtains any termination or rights-reduction remedy on a Sanofi Change of Control. Read against the Change of Control, Acquiror Family and Acquired Party Family definitions in the DEFINITIONS article.

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS governs ownership of Program Inventions, Joint Program Technology and Sanofi Sole Program Patents. Confirm Sanofi owns inventions made by or for it and its data/regulatory filings, that there is no assignment of Sanofi background IP or Sanofi Sole Program Technology to RevMed, and check any reversion/grant-back on termination in sec-p0484.

Test the grant of RevMed Licensed Technology to Sanofi: exclusivity, Field ('any and all uses') and Licensed Territory scope, extension to Affiliates, Sublicensees and Permitted Contractors or Researchers, and that it is not revocable at will (termination only per sec-p0484).

As the paying party we are the audit target: look in FINANCIAL PROVISIONS for RevMed's right to audit Sanofi's Net Sales, Research and Development Costs and Manufacturing Costs records. Check frequency (no more than annually), advance notice, independent-accountant-only access, confidentiality, record-retention period and that RevMed bears the cost absent a material underpayment threshold.

Scan for interest on late payments, diligence-failure penalties or fixed sums payable by Sanofi on missed Development/Commercialization obligations (FINANCIAL PROVISIONS, and remedies in sec-p0484/sec-p0580). Ordinary late-payment interest is not a liquidated-damages deviation; only a punitive fixed sum is.

REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS is the home for RevMed's IP-title, non-infringement, no-encumbrance and compliance warranties, with sec-13.3 carrying its forward-looking covenants. Check for a broad disclaimer of implied warranties and whether any product/manufacturing conformance warranty and remedy exists (cross-check sec-p0357).

The article heading expressly includes INSURANCE; confirm RevMed carries commercial general and clinical-trial/product liability cover at commercially reasonable limits for the Term plus a tail, and that the obligation is at least mutual and evidenced on request.

There is unlikely to be a classic take-or-pay; the analogues are minimum supply/purchase obligations in MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY, committed Research/Development Budget funding, and Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence in the Development and Commercialization articles. Flag only a firm volume or spend commitment on Sanofi with no exit.

Look for consequences-of-termination wind-down in sec-p0484: technology/know-how transfer, transfer or grant of access to Regulatory Approvals and INDs (cross-check the REGULATORY article), transitional supply from RevMed, sell-off rights and return/retention of Confidential Information (see sec-p0451). Direction matters — we want transition assistance running to Sanofi where RevMed terminates or the Product reverts.
